name: OR Lab
intro: Free, interactive tools for the models in the B.B.A. paper Operations Research for Managers. Enter a problem from your textbook or class, and each tool works it out step by step, the way you would by hand, so you can check your own working.

lpp.title: LPP graphical method
lpp.text: Draws every constraint, shades the feasible region, lists the corner points with their Z values and finds the optimum. Spots unbounded, infeasible and multiple-optimum problems, and writes the standard form.

transportation.title: Transportation problem
transportation.text: Initial solutions by the North-West Corner rule, the Least Cost method and Vogel's method, then the MODI method to the optimum, with every table. Handles unbalanced and degenerate problems, profits and blocked routes.

assignment.title: Assignment problem
assignment.text: The Hungarian method step by step: row and column reduction, covering the zeros with the fewest lines, and the optimal assignment. Handles unequal rows and columns, maximisation and blocked cells.

queuing.title: Single-server queue
queuing.text: The M/M/1 model: utilisation, the chance the server is idle, expected numbers in the queue and in the system, waiting times, and the probability of n customers, with each formula shown.

monte-carlo.title: Monte Carlo simulation
monte-carlo.text: Turns a probability table into random-number ranges and simulates with your own random numbers or generated ones. Covers one variable (such as daily demand) and a single-server queue.

games.title: Game theory
games.text: Two-person zero-sum games: maximin and minimax, saddle points, dominance step by step, the 2 × 2 formula and the graphical method for 2 × n and m × 2 games.

network.title: Network Simulator
network.text: CPM and PERT for an arrow diagram: earliest and latest event times, total, free and independent float, every critical path, and the probability of finishing by a date. Then a Monte Carlo simulation runs the project thousands of times.
